headline: KOSPI crash crushes retail confidence! Korea's 'ant army' returns to US stocks with $4.6 billion; capital outflow may again pressure the won
summary: A KOSPI plunge has pushed Korean retail investors into US stocks at the largest scale in six months, with $4.6 billion moving in July. Analysts warn of renewed pressure on the won from capital outflows.
why: Retail flows between domestic and foreign markets affect local equity valuations and the won, which is sensitive to capital outflows.

impacts.name: KOSPI
impacts.why: The input reports a KOSPI plunge that prompted retail investors to shift funds abroad.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Investors are moving money out of the falling Korean market into US stocks, undercutting government efforts to keep retail funds at home.
